4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395 动作: new --- ## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论） # 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner ## 角色 你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。 你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。 你可以使用： - `Read` - `Grep` - `Glob` - 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files` 你不能： - 修改源码 - 写入任何 `.md` 文件 - 输出 JSON 以外的文字 你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。 --- ## 总目标 为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。 这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。 每篇讲义应该满足： 1. 面向初学者也能读懂。 2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。 3. 必须结合真实源码。 4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。 5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。 --- ## 源码探查顺序 请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节： 1. 项目说明 - README - docs - examples - tutorials 2. 构建与运行方式 - package.json - Cargo.toml - pyproject.toml - go.mod - pom.xml - Makefile - Dockerfile - CI 配置 3. 项目入口 - CLI 入口 - Web 服务入口 - main 文件 - library export 文件 - examples 入口 4. 目录结构 - src - lib - app - packages - crates - tests 5. 核心流程 - 初始化流程 - 配置加载 - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路 - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制 6. 测试与示例 - 单元测试 - 集成测试 - benchmark - example usage --- ## 学习路线设计原则 请把学习手册设计成三层： 1. 入门层 beginner 目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。 2. 进阶层 intermediate 目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。 3. 专家层 advanced 目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。 --- ## 讲义拆分规则 - 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。 - 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。 - 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。 - 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。 - 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。 - 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。 - 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。 - 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。 --- ## mode=full 首次生成大纲时： 1. 阅读项目关键文件。 2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。 3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。 4. 输出完整 manifest。 5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。 --- ## mode=incremental 增量更新时： 1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。 2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。 3. 使用： - `git diff previous_head..current_head` - `git log` - `git show` 分析代码变化。 4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。 每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置： - `"keep"` 代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。 - `"update"` 小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。 - `"new"` 新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。 - `"rebuild"` 架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。 如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。 --- ## manifest 输出格式 只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。 ```json { "project": "<项目名>", "head": "", "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。", "units": [ { "id": "u1", "title": "单元标题", "level": "beginner", "order": 1, "lectures": [ { "id": "u1-l1", "title": "讲义标题", "order": 1, "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md", "level": "beginner", "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。", "learning_goals": [ "学习目标 1", "学习目标 2" ], "source_files": [ "README.md", "src/main.ts" ], "minimal_modules": [ "模块 1", "模块 2" ], "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。", "depends_on": [], "action": "new" } ] } ] } ``` --- ## 字段要求 - `project`：项目名。 - `head`：当前 git HEAD。 - `rationale`：中文，一段即可。 - `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。 - `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。 - `filename`： - 必须全局唯一。 - 必须小写。 - 使用连字符。 - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。 - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。 - `level`： - `"beginner"` - `"intermediate"` - `"advanced"` - `source_files`： - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。 - 不要编造文件路径。 - `depends_on`： - 使用讲义 id。 - 没有依赖时填写空数组。 - `action`： - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。 - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。 --- ## 重要约束 - 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。 - 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。 - 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。 - 输出必须是合法 JSON。 ## 完整大纲 ```json { "project": "ground3d-lmm", "rationale": 万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 ` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

标签个数（封顶 2）严格决定该条 QA 的 GT 形状 (num_p_tags, 超点数)，取不到有效 mask 的行用 NaN 占位而非删除，解码器与损失侧均识别并跳过 NaN，永不交付错位 GT。ElasticTransfrom 只生成加噪的体素坐标副本 elastic_coords，不改点也不改任何标签。产出 selected_qa_data 与 sp_gt_seg 逐索引对应，交由下一讲打包。 ### u2-l5 打包与预处理：从 pipeline 到 batch_inputs_dict 本讲是单元2（数据侧）收官：results 字典经 Pack3DDetInputs_Part_Glamm 打包、pseudo_collate 组批、Det3DDataPreprocessor_ 组装，最终成为 loss() 的 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 两个参数。核心结论：数据流分两条物理隔离通道——前向输入走 inputs（训练配置下仅 points、elastic_coords、scene_name、selected_qa_data 四键），监督信号走 data_samples（gt_pts_seg 装 sp_pts_mask 与逐 QA 索引对应的 sp_gt_seg 张量列表）；Pack 按四类键组路由表（INPUTS/SEG/实例键组）分拣，实际打包键＝配置白名单∩results 现有键，未登记新键抛 NotImplementedError，dict/str 列表原样保留以免 QA 文本被 to_tensor 破坏。pseudo_collate 只按位装箱、不堆叠张量，故各值均为按样本的列表，loss() 需用 superpoint_bias/batch_offsets 将各场景超点编号全局化，两条通道最终在 criterion 处汇合。 ### u3-l1 模型主入口 Grounded_LMM_main：init/loss/predict 本讲是 3D 侧入口，解析 Grounded_LMM_main 的三个模块：`__init__` 组件构建、loss() 训练链路、predict() 推理与掩码落盘。核心结论：该类是纯组装者，经 MODELS.build 构建三大组件——SpConvUNet 稀疏卷积主干、Grounded_Decoder_Joint 解码器（内含 Qwen3-VL）、Part3dGlammCriterion_v2 组合损失器；query_thr、set_query_mask、pred_iou 等是继承自 UniSeg3D 的死开关，故训练需 find_unused_parameters=True。loss() 用 superpoint_bias 累计偏移生成 batch_offsets，把各场景超点编号平铺进全局空间，extract_feat 先 scatter_mean 全局池化再按偏移切回逐场景，偏移仅存在于池化一步，GT sp_gt_seg 本就是场景局部故无需平移。predict() 与 loss 共用同段 3D 主干，差异在不传 elastic_coords、GT 保持逐 QA 列表、解码器走 infer_reason_eval 分支；qa_predict_by_feat 以 mask[:, superpoints] 把超点级预测与 GT 上采样到点级，按「有 GT 才对齐、不足补零、超出截断」对齐行数，产出 PointData(qa_pred_masks, qa_gt_masks) 供指标计算，并可经 MASK_DUMP_DIR 落盘 .npy 供可视化。 ### u3-l2 稀疏卷积主干 SpConvUNet 本讲讲解稀疏卷积主干 SpConvUNet（改编自 SPFormer）。点云经 collate 体素化（voxel_size=0.02）后构成 SparseConvTensor 四件套（features、indices、spatial_shape、batch_size），稀疏卷积只对非空体素存储与计算。ResidualBlock 是 pre-norm 双 3×3 SubMConv3d 加恒等跳连：子流形卷积不改变活跃位置，故两支可按行相加；同层卷积共用 indice_key 复用索引规则。SpConvUNet 以递归表达五级 U 形（num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160]），每级含 blocks、conv、u、deconv、blocks_tail 五件套，deconv 与 conv 同键配对实现精确逆映射后再跳连拼接，共四次下采样、总步幅 16。return_blocks=True 返回全分辨率输出与多尺度列表，但 extract_feat 写 `x, _ = self.unet(x)` 丢弃后者，True 仅为解包接口必需；最终输出为与输入活跃位置一致的逐体素 32 通道特征，交由下一讲的超点池化承接。 ### u3-l3 超点池化：collate、scatter_mean 与特征组织 本讲是单元 3 收官，讲清「几十万点 → 几千超点 token」的压缩机制。collate() 把 batch 点云组装成稀疏卷积四件套（coordinates、features、inverse_mapping、spatial_shape）：坐标平移并除以 voxel_size 量化、第 0 列拼样本编号，TensorField.sparse() 做体素去重，inverse_mapping 记录每个点到所在体素的回溯；训练专用 elastic_coords 只替换量化坐标，点特征与逐点标签仍保持对齐。extract_feat() 用一行 scatter_mean 把体素特征经 inverse_mapping 广播回点级、再按全局超点编号分组求均值，得逐超点特征并按 batch_offsets 切回逐场景，它既作 LMM 的 point token 也作分割解码器的 K/V。point_positions 用同一 scatter_mean 对原始米制坐标求超点质心，仅训练且超点数超过 max_point_tokens 时供 FPSPositionAggregator 做 FPS 降采样，推理不聚合。 ### u4-l1 点云 token 注入：PointQwen3VL 的实现技巧 本讲讲解逐超点特征如何注入冻结的 Qwen3-VL 底座：`add_point_embedding` 作为挂在 `language_model` 上的前向预钩子（forward pre-hook），取出 `inputs_embeds` 并校验「`point_mask` 为 True 的个数等于 `point_embeds` 行数」这一数量契约，再用 `masked_scatter` 把 `point2token` 投影后的特征覆盖到 `<|point|>` 占位处，最后返回 `((), kwargs)` 替换模块输入；训练态强制 `requires_grad` 是冻结底座下梯度回传的生命线。文本侧由 `add_special_tokens` 注册 `<|point|>`（`point_token_id` 写回 config）并扩容词表，新行以旧嵌入均值初始化；占位个数与特征行数严格一致，超限先经 FPS 聚合。子类 PointQwen3VLForConditionalGeneration 采用最小覆写加 Auto 注册接入 transformers，`point_mask` 以 `input_ids` 重算，生成仅在预填充步注入。对照 point_qwen2_5_vl 的前向重写式路线（弃视觉塔、三态判断），钩子叠加式零耦合、保留视觉塔，是 Joint（3D+2D）变体的唯一基础。 --- ## 本讲义规格 - id: u4-l2 - 文件名: u4-l2-decoder-init-and-lora.md - 写入路径: ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u4-l2-decoder-init-and-lora.md - 标题: Grounded_Decoder_Joint 初始化与 LoRA 配置 - 学习阶段: intermediate - 主题: 分析解码器 __init__ 中的 point2token、query_proj 投影层，_init_reason_model 的词表扩容与 LoRA 注入（get_peft_model），以及 FPS 聚合器。 - 学习目标: 说明 point2token/query_proj 的维度变换（256 ↔ hidden_size）；解释 get_target_modules 按 lora_type 筛选注入层；统计 LoRA 可训练参数占比 - 应覆盖的最小模块: point2token / query_proj 投影层，_init_reason_model 与特殊 token 词表扩容，LoRA 注入与可训练参数统计，FPS/位置 FPS 聚合器 - 关键源码: uniseg3d/query_decoder.py，configs/ground3dlmm_train.py - 代码实践任务: 由 worker 根据主题和源码自行设计 - 依赖讲义: u3-l3 --- ## 任务 请按照 worker prompt 生成这一篇讲义。 要求： 1. 只生成 `ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u4-l2-decoder-init-and-lora.md` 这一个文件。 2. 必须结合真实源码。 3. 必须包含代码实践。 4. 必须使用永久链接引用源码。 5. new/rebuild 万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 token（`<|point|>` 与 ``）、OpenMMLab 配置注册机制。 ### u1-l2 环境搭建：OpenMMLab 栈与 MinkowskiEngine 安装 本讲覆盖四个最小模块：conda 环境与依赖清单、mmcv 源码编译、MinkowskiEngine 源码编译、本包安装与依赖验证。核心结论：Ground3D-LMM 同时依赖 OpenMMLab 四层栈（mmengine→mmcv→mmdet→mmdet3d）、稀疏卷积库 spconv 与 MinkowskiEngine、以及 LLM 栈（transformers/peft），含 CUDA 算子的包必须与 PyTorch 版本、CUDA 工具链、GPU 架构三方对齐，官方锁定 torch2.4.1+cu118；environment.yml 刻意不完整，mmcv/mmdet3d/MinkowskiEngine 须按 Option B 手动源码补装，要点为关闭构建隔离、setuptools<70、ME 从 master 分支编译。本讲引入的关键术语：构建隔离、稀疏卷积、ME 的稀疏批组装与坐标量化（后续超点池化的基础设施）、LoRA/peft、editable 安装。验证方法论是以 import uniseg3d 成功为准而非文档清单，可暴露文档未列的隐藏依赖。 ### u1-l3 仓库结构与 OpenMMLab 注册机制 本讲梳理仓库分层与 OpenMMLab 注册机制。仓库为插件式：configs/ 只写声明，uniseg3d/ 只写实现，tools/ 仅 train.py 与 test.py 构建 Runner，data/ 由用户填充。「注册表」把配置中的 type 字符串映射为真实类：custom_imports 触发导入 uniseg3d，靠 import 副作用执行各模块顶层 register_module 完成注册；注册名默认即类名，尾下划线为继承上游的改版类。mmengine Config 支持 _base_ 跨包继承、递归覆盖与 _delete_ 重建，_3d 变体仅覆盖 3 个字段即成完整配置；--cfg-options 点路径数字即列表下标。 ### u1-l4 快速上手：用预训练权重跑一次接地推理 本讲以复现 README 快速上手为主线，覆盖三个模块：tools/test.py 执行主线、评估配置的任务切换旋钮、预测 JSON 产物结构。核心结论：test.py 是 mmdet3d 通用测试入口，不含任何模型特有逻辑，配置驱动、CLI 优先——`--cfg-options` 按点路径合并进配置（数字即列表下标），checkpoint 位置参数无条件覆盖 `load_from`。评估任务由 `QA_Generation_Test` 的三层旋钮 `task_level`/`task_type`/`sub_task` 决定，None 表示该层不过滤，过滤是严格匹配、拼错静默为空；点路径 `pipeline.2.transforms.2` 的两个下标分别指向 `MultiScaleFlipAug3D` 与该变换；`save_pred_qa_dir` 开启逐场景文本预测 JSON（question/gt_answer/pred_answer 三字段，多轮加 turn_idx），由解码器在 `infer_reason_eval` 中直接写盘；分割 mIoU 则由 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 聚合，两条输出通道相互独立，JSON 不含掩码且写盘先于分割解码。关键术语：checkpoint、snapshot_download、TestLoop、`

` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

标签个数（封顶 2）严格决定该条 QA 的 GT 形状 (num_p_tags, 超点数)，取不到有效 mask 的行用 NaN 占位而非删除，解码器与损失侧均识别并跳过 NaN，永不交付错位 GT。ElasticTransfrom 只生成加噪的体素坐标副本 elastic_coords，不改点也不改任何标签。产出 selected_qa_data 与 sp_gt_seg 逐索引对应，交由下一讲打包。 ### u2-l5 打包与预处理：从 pipeline 到 batch_inputs_dict 本讲是单元2（数据侧）收官：results 字典经 Pack3DDetInputs_Part_Glamm 打包、pseudo_collate 组批、Det3DDataPreprocessor_ 组装，最终成为 loss() 的 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 两个参数。核心结论：数据流分两条物理隔离通道——前向输入走 inputs（训练配置下仅 points、elastic_coords、scene_name、selected_qa_data 四键），监督信号走 data_samples（gt_pts_seg 装 sp_pts_mask 与逐 QA 索引对应的 sp_gt_seg 张量列表）；Pack 按四类键组路由表（INPUTS/SEG/实例键组）分拣，实际打包键＝配置白名单∩results 现有键，未登记新键抛 NotImplementedError，dict/str 列表原样保留以免 QA 文本被 to_tensor 破坏。pseudo_collate 只按位装箱、不堆叠张量，故各值均为按样本的列表，loss() 需用 superpoint_bias/batch_offsets 将各场景超点编号全局化，两条通道最终在 criterion 处汇合。 ### u3-l1 模型主入口 Grounded_LMM_main：init/loss/predict 本讲是 3D 侧入口，解析 Grounded_LMM_main 的三个模块：`__init__` 组件构建、loss() 训练链路、predict() 推理与掩码落盘。核心结论：该类是纯组装者，经 MODELS.build 构建三大组件——SpConvUNet 稀疏卷积主干、Grounded_Decoder_Joint 解码器（内含 Qwen3-VL）、Part3dGlammCriterion_v2 组合损失器；query_thr、set_query_mask、pred_iou 等是继承自 UniSeg3D 的死开关，故训练需 find_unused_parameters=True。loss() 用 superpoint_bias 累计偏移生成 batch_offsets，把各场景超点编号平铺进全局空间，extract_feat 先 scatter_mean 全局池化再按偏移切回逐场景，偏移仅存在于池化一步，GT sp_gt_seg 本就是场景局部故无需平移。predict() 与 loss 共用同段 3D 主干，差异在不传 elastic_coords、GT 保持逐 QA 列表、解码器走 infer_reason_eval 分支；qa_predict_by_feat 以 mask[:, superpoints] 把超点级预测与 GT 上采样到点级，按「有 GT 才对齐、不足补零、超出截断」对齐行数，产出 PointData(qa_pred_masks, qa_gt_masks) 供指标计算，并可经 MASK_DUMP_DIR 落盘 .npy 供可视化。 ### u3-l2 稀疏卷积主干 SpConvUNet 本讲讲解稀疏卷积主干 SpConvUNet（改编自 SPFormer）。点云经 collate 体素化（voxel_size=0.02）后构成 SparseConvTensor 四件套（features、indices、spatial_shape、batch_size），稀疏卷积只对非空体素存储与计算。ResidualBlock 是 pre-norm 双 3×3 SubMConv3d 加恒等跳连：子流形卷积不改变活跃位置，故两支可按行相加；同层卷积共用 indice_key 复用索引规则。SpConvUNet 以递归表达五级 U 形（num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160]），每级含 blocks、conv、u、deconv、blocks_tail 五件套，deconv 与 conv 同键配对实现精确逆映射后再跳连拼接，共四次下采样、总步幅 16。return_blocks=True 返回全分辨率输出与多尺度列表，但 extract_feat 写 `x, _ = self.unet(x)` 丢弃后者，True 仅为解包接口必需；最终输出为与输入活跃位置一致的逐体素 32 通道特征，交由下一讲的超点池化承接。 ### u3-l3 超点池化：collate、scatter_mean 与特征组织 本讲是单元 3 收官，讲清「几十万点 → 几千超点 token」的压缩机制。collate() 把 batch 点云组装成稀疏卷积四件套（coordinates、features、inverse_mapping、spatial_shape）：坐标平移并除以 voxel_size 量化、第 0 列拼样本编号，TensorField.sparse() 做体素去重，inverse_mapping 记录每个点到所在体素的回溯；训练专用 elastic_coords 只替换量化坐标，点特征与逐点标签仍保持对齐。extract_feat() 用一行 scatter_mean 把体素特征经 inverse_mapping 广播回点级、再按全局超点编号分组求均值，得逐超点特征并按 batch_offsets 切回逐场景，它既作 LMM 的 point tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395 动作: new --- ## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论） # 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner ## 角色 你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。 你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。 你可以使用： - `Read` - `Grep` - `Glob` - 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git 构建与运行方式 - package.json - Cargo.toml - pyproject.toml - go.mod - pom.xml - Makefile - Dockerfile - CI 配置 3. 项目入口 - CLI 入口 - Web 服务入口 - main 文件 - library export 文件 - examples 入口 4. 目录结构 - src - lib - app - packages - crates - tests 5. 核心流程 - 初始化流程 - 配置加载 - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路 - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制 6. 测试与示例 - 单元测试 - 集成测试 - benchmark - example usage --- ## 学习路线设计原则 请把学习手册设计成三层： 1. 入门层 beginner 万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 token（`<|point|>` 与 ``）、OpenMMLab 配置注册机制。 ### u1-l2 环境搭建：OpenMMLab 栈与 MinkowskiEngine 安装 本讲覆盖四个最小模块：conda 环境与依赖清单、mmcv 源码编译、MinkowskiEngine 源码编译、本包安装与依赖验证。核心结论：Ground3D-LMM 同时依赖 OpenMMLab 四层栈（mmengine→mmcv→mmdet→mmdet3d）、稀疏卷积库 spconv 与 MinkowskiEngine、以及 LLM 栈（transformers/peft），含 CUDA 算子的包必须与 PyTorch 版本、CUDA 工具链、GPU 架构三方对齐，官方锁定 torch2.4.1+cu118；environment.yml 刻意不完整，mmcv/mmdet3d/MinkowskiEngine 须按 Option B 手动源码补装，要点为关闭构建隔离、setuptools<70、ME 从 master 分支编译。本讲引入的关键术语：构建隔离、稀疏卷积、ME 的稀疏批组装与坐标量化（后续超点池化的基础设施）、LoRA/peft、editable 安装。验证方法论是以 import uniseg3d 成功为准而非文档清单，可暴露文档未列的隐藏依赖。 ### u1-l3 仓库结构与 OpenMMLab 注册机制 本讲梳理仓库分层与 OpenMMLab 注册机制。仓库为插件式：configs/ 只写声明，uniseg3d/ 只写实现，tools/ 仅 train.py 与 test.py 构建 Runner，data/ 由用户填充。「注册表」把配置中的 type 字符串映射为真实类：custom_imports 触发导入 uniseg3d，靠 import 副作用执行各模块顶层 register_module 完成注册；注册名默认即类名，尾下划线为继承上游的改版类。mmengine Config 支持 _base_ 跨包继承、递归覆盖与 _delete_ 重建，_3d 变体仅覆盖 3 个字段即成完整配置；--cfg-options 点路径数字即列表下标。 ### u1-l4 快速上手：用预训练权重跑一次接地推理 本讲以复现 README 快速上手为主线，覆盖三个模块：tools/test.py 执行主线、评估配置的任务切换旋钮、预测 JSON 产物结构。核心结论：test.py 是 mmdet3d 通用测试入口，不含任何模型特有逻辑，配置驱动、CLI 优先——`--cfg-options` 按点路径合并进配置（数字即列表下标），checkpoint 位置参数无条件覆盖 `load_from`。评估任务由 `QA_Generation_Test` 的三层旋钮 `task_level`/`task_type`/`sub_task` 决定，None 表示该层不过滤，过滤是严格匹配、拼错静默为空；点路径 `pipeline.2.transforms.2` 的两个下标分别指向 `MultiScaleFlipAug3D` 与该变换；`save_pred_qa_dir` 开启逐场景文本预测 JSON（question/gt_answer/pred_answer 三字段，多轮加 turn_idx），由解码器在 `infer_reason_eval` 中直接写盘；分割 mIoU 则由 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 聚合，两条输出通道相互独立，JSON 不含掩码且写盘先于分割解码。关键术语：checkpoint、snapshot_download、TestLoop、`

` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

标签个数（封顶 2）严格决定该条 QA 的 GT 形状 (num_p_tags, 超点数)，取不到有效 mask 的行用 NaN 占位而非删除，解码器与损失侧均识别并跳过 NaN，永不交付错位 GT。ElasticTransfrom 只生成加噪的体素坐标副本 elastic_coords，不改点也不改任何标签。产出 selected_qa_data 与 sp_gt_seg 逐索引对应，交由下一讲打包。 ### u2-l5 打包与预处理：从 pipeline 到 batch_inputs_dict 本讲是单元2（数据侧）收官：results 字典经 Pack3DDetInputs_Part_Glamm 打包、pseudo_collate 组批、Det3DDataPreprocessor_ 组装，最终成为 loss() 的 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 两个参数。核心结论：数据流分两条物理隔离通道——前向输入走 inputs（训练配置下仅 points、elastic_coords、scene_name、selected_qa_data 四键），监督信号走 data_samples（gt_pts_seg 装 sp_pts_mask 与逐 QA 索引对应的 sp_gt_seg 张量列表）；Pack 将各场景超点编号全局化，两条通道最终在 criterion 处汇合。 ### u3-l1 模型主入口 Grounded_LMM_main：init/loss/predict 本讲是 3D 侧入口，解析 Grounded_LMM_main 的三个模块：`__init__` 组件构建、loss() 训练链路、predict() 推理与掩码落盘。核心结论：该类是纯组装者，经 MODELS.build token 也作分割解码器的 K/V。point_positions 用同一 scatter_mean 对原始米制坐标求超点质心，仅训练且超点数超过 max_point_tokens 时供 FPSPositionAggregator 做 FPS 降采样，推理不聚合。 ### u4-l1 点云 token 注入：PointQwen3VL 的实现技巧 本讲讲解逐超点特征如何注入冻结的 Qwen3-VL 33	def preprocess_chatml(input_ids, text, tokenizer, qwen_model='qwen3_vl'):
34	    """Build training labels from a ChatML conversation.
35	
36	    Loss is computed **only on the assistant replies**: every other span
37	    (system prompt, user turns, role headers) is masked with ``IGNORE_INDEX``,
38	    as is the trailing incomplete assistant turn (the generation prompt).
39	
40	    Args:
41	        input_ids (torch.Tensor): ``(1, L)`` token ids of the full conversation.
42	        text (str): the same conversation as a string (used to split rounds).
43	        tokenizer: the LMM tokenizer (``self.processor.tokenizer``).
44	        qwen_model (str): ``'qwen2_5_vl'`` or ``'qwen3_vl'`` — selects the
45	            ChatML system prompt via :func:`~uniseg3d.conversation.get_conv`.
46	
47	    Returns:
48	        torch.Tensor: labels shaped like ``input_ids``, masked with ``IGNORE_INDEX``.
49	    """
50	    conv = get_conv('chatml', qwen_model=qwen_model)
51	    rounds = [m + conv.seps[0] for m in text.split(conv.seps[0])]
52	
53	    # the final chunk is the incomplete assistant turn -> never supervised
54	    last_invalide_text = rounds[-1]
55	    rounds = rounds[:-1]
56	
57	    if conv.system is None:
58	        rounds = [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(0, len(rounds), 2)]
59	    else:
60	        rounds = [''.join(rounds[:3])] + [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(3, len(rounds), 2)]
61	
62	    labels = input_ids.clone()
63	
64	    sep = conv.seps[0] + conv.roles[1]
65	    cur_len = 0
66	
67	    for rou in rounds:
68	        if len(rou) == 0:
69	            break
70	
71	        # mask everything up to and including the assistant header
72	        ins = sep.join(rou.split(sep)[:-1]) + sep
73	        rou_len = tokenizer(rou, return_length=True).length[0]
74	        ins_len = tokenizer(ins, return_length=True).length[0]
75	        labels[:, cur_len:cur_len + ins_len] = IGNORE_INDEX
76	        cur_len += rou_len
77	
78	    if (labels == IGNORE_INDEX).sum() == labels.size(1):
79	        raise ValueError('No valid labels found')
80	
81	    last_invalide = tokenizer(last_invalide_text, return_length=True).length[0]
82	    labels[:, -last_invalide + 1:] = IGNORE_INDEX
83	
84	    return labels

87	class ConvSetAggregator(nn.Module):
88	    """Aggregate variable-length point features into a fixed number of tokens
89	    using 1D convolution across the set dimension followed by adaptive pooling.
90	
91	    Args:
92	        in_channels (int): Feature dimension per point.
93	        out_tokens (int): Number of aggregated tokens.
94	        kernel_size (int): Convolution kernel size for the first layer.
95	        hidden_channels (int | None): Hidden channels; defaults to in_channels.
96	    """
97	    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_tokens, kernel_size=5, hidden_channels=None):
98	        super().__init__()
99	        hidden = in_channels if hidden_channels is None else hidden_channels
100	        padding = kernel_size // 2
101	        self.net = nn.Sequential(
102	            nn.Conv1d(in_channels, hidden, kernel_size=kernel_size, padding=padding),
103	            nn.GELU(),
104	            nn.Conv1d(hidden, in_channels, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
105	            nn.GELU(),
106	        )
107	        self.pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool1d(out_tokens)
108	
109	    def forward(self, x):
110	        # x: (N, D)
111	        if x.dim() != 2:
112	            raise ValueError('ConvSetAggregator expects 2D tensor of shape (N, D)')
113	        n, d = x.shape
114	        x1 = x.transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(0)  # (1, D, N)
115	        y = self.net(x1)
116	        y = self.pool(y)  # (1, D, K)
117	        y = y.squeeze(0).transpose(0, 1)  # (K, D)
118	        return y

120	class PositionSoftClusterAggregator(nn.Module):
121	    """Position-aware soft clustering aggregator.
122	
123	    Aggregates features into K tokens using soft assignment based on
124	    Euclidean distance between normalized point positions and learnable
125	    prototype centers. Permutation-invariant and driven by spatial layout.
126	
127	    Args:
128	        in_channels (int): Feature dimension per point.
129	        out_tokens (int): Number of aggregated tokens (cluster centers).
130	        pos_dim (int): Dimensionality of positions (default 3).
131	        temperature (float): Softmax temperature over negative distances.
132	    """
133	    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_tokens, pos_dim=3, temperature=0.5):
134	        super().__init__()
135	        self.out_tokens = out_tokens
136	        self.temperature = temperature
137	        self.register_parameter(
138	            'centers', nn.Parameter(torch.randn(out_tokens, pos_dim)))
139	
140	    def forward(self, feats, pos):
141	        # feats: (N, D), pos: (N, P)
142	        if feats.dim() != 2 or pos.dim() != 2:
143	            raise ValueError('PositionSoftClusterAggregator expects 2D tensors (N, D) and (N, P)')
144	        if feats.shape[0] != pos.shape[0]:
145	            raise ValueError('feats and pos must have same first dimension N')
146	        # normalize positions per-sample
147	        p = pos.float()
148	        p = p - p.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
149	        std = p.std(dim=0, keepdim=True) + 1e-6
150	        p = p / std
151	        # distances to centers: (N, K)
152	        diff = p.unsqueeze(1) - self.centers.unsqueeze(0)
153	        dist = (diff ** 2).sum(-1)
154	        assign = torch.softmax(-dist / max(self.temperature, 1e-6), dim=1)  # (N, K)
155	        # aggregate features: (K, D)
156	        num = assign.sum(dim=0, keepdim=True).transpose(0, 1) + 1e-6  # (K, 1)
157	        agg = assign.transpose(0, 1) @ feats  # (K, D)
158	        agg = agg / num
159	        return agg

162	class FPSAggregator(nn.Module):
163	    """Farthest Point Sampling (FPS) aggregator.
164	    
165	    Samples a fixed number of points using FPS algorithm based on feature distances.
166	    
167	    Args:
168	        in_channels (int): Feature dimension per point (not used, kept for compatibility).
169	        out_tokens (int): Number of sampled points.
170	    """
171	    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_tokens):
172	        super().__init__()
173	        self.out_tokens = out_tokens
174	    
175	    def forward(self, x):
176	        # x: (N, D)
177	        if x.dim() != 2:
178	            raise ValueError('FPSAggregator expects 2D tensor of shape (N, D)')
179	        n, d = x.shape
180	        
181	        if n <= self.out_tokens:
182	            return x
183	        
184	        # FPS sampling based on feature L2 distances
185	        indices = self.fps_sample(x, self.out_tokens)
186	        return x[indices]
187	    
188	    @staticmethod
189	    def fps_sample(points, num_samples):
190	        """Farthest Point Sampling.
191	        
192	        Args:
193	            points: (N, D) tensor
194	            num_samples: number of samples to select
195	            
196	        Returns:
197	            indices: (num_samples,) tensor of selected indices
198	        """
199	        n = points.shape[0]
200	        device = points.device
201	        
202	        # Start with a random point
203	        indices = torch.zeros(num_samples, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
204	        distances = torch.ones(n, device=device) * float('inf')
205	        
206	        # Compute pairwise distances
207	        dist_matrix = torch.cdist(points, points)  # (N, N)
208	        
209	        # First point: random
210	        current = torch.randint(0, n, (1,), device=device).item()
211	        indices[0] = current
212	        
213	        for i in range(1, num_samples):
214	            # Update distances to the current farthest point
215	            dist_to_current = dist_matrix[current]  # (N,)
216	            distances = torch.minimum(distances, dist_to_current)
217	            
218	            # Select the farthest point
219	            current = distances.argmax().item()
220	            indices[i] = current
221	        
222	        return indices

292	def mask_pool(x, mask):
293	    """
294	    Args:
295	        x: [D, M]
296	        mask: [N, M]
297	    """
298	    with torch.no_grad():
299	        mask = mask.detach()
300	        mask = (mask > 0).to(mask.dtype)
301	        denorm = mask.sum(dim=(-1), keepdim=True) + 1e-8
302	
303	    mask_pooled_x = torch.einsum(
304	        "dm,nm->nd",
305	        x,
306	        mask / denorm,
307	    )
308	    return mask_pooled_x

345	                each of shape (n_queries, n_points).
346	        
347	        Return:
348	            List[Tensor]: Queries of len batch_size,
349	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
350	        """
351	        outputs = []
352	        for i in range(len(sources)):
353	            k = v = sources[i]
354	            attn_mask = attn_masks[i] if attn_masks is not None else None
355	            output, _ = self.attn(queries[i], k, v, attn_mask=attn_mask)
356	            if self.fix:
357	                output = self.dropout(output)
358	            output = output + queries[i]
359	            if self.fix:
360	                output = self.norm(output)
361	            outputs.append(output)
362	        return outputs

365	class SelfAttentionLayer(BaseModule):
366	    """Self attention layer.
367	
368	    Args:
369	        d_model (int): Model dimension.
370	        num_heads (int): Number of heads.
371	        dropout (float): Dropout rate.
372	    """
373	
374	    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads, dropout):
375	        super().__init__()
376	        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(
377	            d_model, num_heads, dropout=dropout, batch_first=True)
378	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
379	        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
380	
381	    def forward(self, x, interaction_masks=None):
382	        """Forward pass.
383	
384	        Args:
385	            x (List[Tensor]): Queries of len batch_size,
386	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
387	        
388	        Returns:
389	            List[Tensor]: Queries of len batch_size,
390	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
391	        """
392	        out = []
393	
394	
395	        
396	
397	        for i, y in enumerate(x):
398	            nan_mask = torch.isnan(y).any(dim=-1)  # shape: (num_queries,)
399	        
400	            # replace NaN with 0
401	            y_safe = y.clone()
402	            y_safe[nan_mask] = 0.0
403	            if not interaction_masks:
404	                z, _ = self.attn(y_safe, y_safe, y_safe)
405	            else:
406	                z, _ = self.attn(y_safe, y_safe, y_safe, attn_mask=interaction_masks[i])
407	            z = self.dropout(z) + y
408	            z = self.norm(z)
409	            out.append(z)
410	        return out

413	class FFN(BaseModule):
414	    """Feed forward network.
415	
416	    Args:
417	        d_model (int): Model dimension.
418	        hidden_dim (int): Hidden dimension.
419	        dropout (float): Dropout rate.
420	        activation_fn (str): 'relu' or 'gelu'.
421	    """
422	
423	    def __init__(self, d_model, hidden_dim, dropout, activation_fn):
424	        super().__init__()
425	        self.net = nn.Sequential(
426	            nn.Linear(d_model, hidden_dim),
427	            nn.ReLU() if activation_fn == 'relu' else nn.GELU(),
428	            nn.Dropout(dropout),
429	            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, d_model),
430	            nn.Dropout(dropout))
431	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
432	
433	    def forward(self, x):
434	        """Forward pass.
435	
436	        Args:
437	            x (List[Tensor]): Queries of len batch_size,
438	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
439	        
440	        Returns:
441	            List[Tensor]: Queries of len batch_size,
442	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
443	        """
444	        out = []
445	        for y in x:
446	            z = self.net(y)
447	            z = z + y
448	            z = self.norm(z)
449	            out.append(z)
450	        return out

453	class QueryDecoder(BaseModule):
454	    """Query decoder.
455	
456	    Args:
457	        num_layers (int): Number of transformer layers.
458	        num_instance_queries (int): Number of instance queries.
459	        num_semantic_queries (int): Number of semantic queries.
460	        num_classes (int): Number of classes.
461	        in_channels (int): Number of input channels.
462	        d_model (int): Number of channels for model layers.
463	        num_heads (int): Number of head in attention layer.
464	        hidden_dim (int): Dimension of attention layer.
465	        dropout (float): Dropout rate for transformer layer.
466	        activation_fn (str): 'relu' of 'gelu'.
467	        iter_pred (bool): Whether to predict iteratively.
468	        attn_mask (bool): Whether to use mask attention.
469	        pos_enc_flag (bool): Whether to use positional enconding.
470	    """
471	
472	    def __init__(self, num_layers, num_instance_queries, num_semantic_queries,
473	                 num_classes, in_channels, d_model, num_heads, hidden_dim,
474	                 dropout, activation_fn, iter_pred, attn_mask, fix_attention,
475	                 objectness_flag, sphere_cls, **kwargs):
476	        super().__init__()
477	        self.objectness_flag = objectness_flag
478	        self.sphere_cls = sphere_cls
479	        self.input_proj = nn.Sequential(
480	            nn.Linear(in_channels, d_model), nn.LayerNorm(d_model), nn.ReLU())
481	        self.num_queries = num_instance_queries + num_semantic_queries
482	        if num_instance_queries + num_semantic_queries > 0:
483	            self.query = nn.Embedding(num_instance_queries + num_semantic_queries, d_model)
484	        if num_instance_queries == 0:
485	            self.query_proj = nn.Sequential(
486	                nn.Linear(in_channels, d_model), nn.ReLU(),
487	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model))
488	        self.cross_attn_layers = nn.ModuleList([])
489	        self.self_attn_layers = nn.ModuleList([])
490	        self.ffn_layers = nn.ModuleList([])
491	        for i in range(num_layers):
492	            self.cross_attn_layers.append(
493	                CrossAttentionLayer(
494	                    d_model, num_heads, dropout, fix_attention))
495	            self.self_attn_layers.append(
496	                SelfAttentionLayer(d_model, num_heads, dropout))
497	            self.ffn_layers.append(
498	                FFN(d_model, hidden_dim, dropout, activation_fn))
499	        self.out_norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
500	        if not self.sphere_cls:
501	            self.out_cls = nn.Sequential(
502	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(),
503	                nn.Linear(d_model, num_classes + 1))
504	        if objectness_flag:
505	            self.out_score = nn.Sequential(
506	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(d_model, 1))
507	        self.x_mask = nn.Sequential(
508	            nn.Linear(in_channels, d_model), nn.ReLU(),
509	            nn.Linear(d_model, d_model))
510	        self.iter_pred = iter_pred
511	        self.attn_mask = attn_mask
512	    
513	    def _get_queries(self, queries=None, batch_size=None):
514	        """Get query tensor.
515	
516	        Args:
517	            queries (List[Tensor], optional): of len batch_size,
518	                each of shape (n_queries_i, in_channels).
519	            batch_size (int, optional): batch size.
520	        
521	        Returns:
522	            List[Tensor]: of len batch_size, each of shape
523	                (n_queries_i, d_model).
524	        """
525	        if batch_size is None:
526	            batch_size = len(queries)
527	        
528	        result_queries = []
529	        for i in range(batch_size):
530	            result_query = []
531	            if hasattr(self, 'query'):
532	                result_query.append(self.query.weight)
533	            if queries is not None:
534	                result_query.append(self.query_proj(queries[i]))
535	            result_queries.append(torch.cat(result_query))
536	        return result_queries
537	
538	    def _forward_head(self, queries, mask_feats):
539	        """Prediction head forward.
540	
541	        Args:
542	            queries (List[Tensor] | Tensor): List of len batch_size,
543	                each of shape (n_queries_i, d_model). Or tensor of
544	                shape (batch_size, n_queries, d_model).
545	            mask_feats (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size,
546	                each of shape (n_points_i, d_model).
547	
548	        Returns:
549	            Tuple:
550	                List[Tensor]: Classification predictions of len batch_size,
551	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_classes + 1).
552	                List[Tensor]: Confidence scores of len batch_size,
553	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, 1).
554	                List[Tensor]: Predicted masks of len batch_size,
555	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_points_i).
556	                List[Tensor] or None: Attention masks of len batch_size,
557	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_points_i).
558	        """
559	        cls_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks = [], [], [], []
560	        for i in range(len(queries)):
561	            norm_query = self.out_norm(queries[i])
562	            cls_preds.append(self.out_cls(norm_query))
563	            pred_score = self.out_score(norm_query) if self.objectness_flag \
564	                else None
565	            pred_scores.append(pred_score)
566	            pred_mask = torch.einsum('nd,md->nm', norm_query, mask_feats[i])
567	            if self.attn_mask:
568	                attn_mask = (pred_mask.sigmoid() < 0.5).bool()
569	                attn_mask[torch.where(
570	                    attn_mask.sum(-1) == attn_mask.shape[-1])] = False
571	                attn_mask = attn_mask.detach()
572	                attn_masks.append(attn_mask)
573	            pred_masks.append(pred_mask)
574	        attn_masks = attn_masks if self.attn_mask else None
575	        return cls_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks
576	
577	    def forward_simple(self, x, queries):
578	        """Simple forward pass.
579	        
580	        Args:
581	            x (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size, each of shape
582	                (n_points_i, in_channels).
583	            queries (List[Tensor], optional): of len batch_size, each of shape
584	                (n_points_i, in_channles).
585	        
586	        Returns:
587	            Dict: with labels, masks, and scores.
588	        """
589	        inst_feats = [self.input_proj(y) for y in x]
590	        mask_feats = [self.x_mask(y) for y in x]
591	        queries = self._get_queries(queries, len(x))
592	        for i in range(len(self.cross_attn_layers)):
593	            queries = self.cross_attn_layers[i](inst_feats, queries)
594	            queries = self.self_attn_layers[i](queries)
595	            queries = self.ffn_layers[i](queries)
596	        cls_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, _ = self._forward_head(
597	            queries, mask_feats)
598	        return dict(
599	            cls_preds=cls_preds,
600	            masks=pred_masks,
601	            scores=pred_scores)
602	
603	    def forward_iter_pred(self, x, queries):
604	        """Iterative forward pass.
605	        
606	        Args:
607	            x (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size, each of shape
608	                (n_points_i, in_channels).
609	            queries (List[Tensor], optional): of len batch_size, each of shape
610	                (n_points_i, in_channles).
611	        
612	        Returns:
613	            Dict: with labels, masks, scores, and aux_outputs.
614	        """
615	        cls_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks = [], [], []
616	        inst_feats = [self.input_proj(y) for y in x]
617	        mask_feats = [self.x_mask(y) for y in x]
618	        queries = self._get_queries(queries, len(x))
619	        cls_pred, pred_score, pred_mask, attn_mask = self._forward_head(
620	            queries, mask_feats)
621	        cls_preds.append(cls_pred)
622	        pred_scores.append(pred_score)
623	        pred_masks.append(pred_mask)
624	        for i in range(len(self.cross_attn_layers)):
625	            queries = self.cross_attn_layers[i](inst_feats, queries, attn_mask)
626	            queries = self.self_attn_layers[i](queries)
627	            queries = self.ffn_layers[i](queries)
628	            cls_pred, pred_score, pred_mask, attn_mask = self._forward_head(
629	                queries, mask_feats)
630	            cls_preds.append(cls_pred)
631	            pred_scores.append(pred_score)
632	            pred_masks.append(pred_mask)
633	
634	        aux_outputs = [
635	            {'cls_preds': cls_pred, 'masks': masks, 'scores': scores}
636	            for cls_pred, scores, masks in zip(
637	                cls_preds[:-1], pred_scores[:-1], pred_masks[:-1])]
638	        return dict(
639	            cls_preds=cls_preds[-1],
640	            masks=pred_masks[-1],
641	            scores=pred_scores[-1],
642	            aux_outputs=aux_outputs)
643	
644	    def forward(self, x, queries=None, interaction_masks=None):
645	        """Forward pass.
646	        
647	        Args:
648	            x (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size, each of shape
649	                (n_points_i, in_channels).
650	            queries (List[Tensor], optional): of len batch_size, each of shape
651	                (n_points_i, in_channles).
652	        
653	        Returns:
654	            Dict: with labels, masks, scores, and possibly aux_outputs.
655	        """
656	        if self.iter_pred:
657	            return self.forward_iter_pred(x, queries, interaction_masks=interaction_masks)
658	        else:
659	            return self.forward_simple(x, queries)

663	class UnifiedQueryDecoder(QueryDecoder):
664	    """We simply add semantic prediction for each instance query.
665	    """
666	    def __init__(self, num_instance_classes, num_semantic_classes,
667	                 d_model, num_semantic_linears, sphere_cls, vocabulary_cls_embedding_path, **kwargs):
668	        super().__init__(
669	            num_classes=num_instance_classes, d_model=d_model, sphere_cls= sphere_cls, **kwargs)
670	        if not self.sphere_cls:
671	            assert num_semantic_linears in [1, 2]
672	            if num_semantic_linears == 2:
673	                self.out_sem = nn.Sequential(
674	                    nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(),
675	                    nn.Linear(d_model, num_semantic_classes + 1))
676	            else:
677	                self.out_sem = nn.Linear(d_model, num_semantic_classes + 1)
678	            
679	        if self.sphere_cls:
680	            rank, world_size = get_dist_info()
681	            cls_embed = torch.load(vocabulary_cls_embedding_path)
682	            
683	            _dim = cls_embed.size(2)
684	            _prototypes = cls_embed.size(1)
685	
686	            if rank == 0:
687	                back_token = torch.zeros(1, _dim, dtype=torch.float32, device='cuda')
688	            else:
689	                back_token = torch.empty(1, _dim, dtype=torch.float32, device='cuda')
690	            if world_size > 1:
691	                dist.broadcast(back_token, src=0)
692	            back_token = back_token.to(device='cpu')
693	            cls_embed = torch.cat([
694	                cls_embed, back_token.repeat(_prototypes, 1)[None]
695	            ], dim=0)
696	            self.register_buffer('cls_embed', cls_embed.permute(2, 0, 1).contiguous(), persistent=False)
697	            
698	            cls_embed_dim = self.cls_embed.size(0)
699	            self.cls_proj = nn.Sequential(
700	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
701	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
702	                nn.Linear(d_model, cls_embed_dim))
703	            
704	            self.cls_proj_sem = nn.Sequential(
705	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
706	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
707	                nn.Linear(d_model, cls_embed_dim))
708	            
709	            logit_scale = torch.tensor(4.6052, dtype=torch.float32)
710	            self.register_buffer('logit_scale', logit_scale, persistent=False)
711	            
712	            # Mask Pooling
713	            self.mask_pooling = mask_pool
714	            self.mask_pooling_proj = nn.Sequential(
715	                nn.LayerNorm(d_model),
716	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
717	            )
718	            
719	            self.mask_pooling_proj_sem = nn.Sequential(
720	                nn.LayerNorm(d_model),
721	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
722	            )
723	    def forward_logit(self, cls_embd, sem=False):
724	        if sem:
725	            cls_pred = torch.einsum('nd,dkp->nkp', F.normalize(cls_embd, dim=-1), self.cls_embed)
726	        else:
727	            cls_pred = torch.einsum('nd,dkp->nkp', F.normalize(cls_embd, dim=-1), self.cls_embed[:, 2:, :])
728	        cls_pred = cls_pred.max(-1).values
729	        cls_pred = self.logit_scale.exp() * cls_pred
730	        return cls_pred
731	    
732	    def _forward_head(self, queries, mask_feats, last_flag):
733	        """Prediction head forward.
734	
735	        Args:
736	            queries (List[Tensor] | Tensor): List of len batch_size,
737	                each of shape (n_queries_i, d_model). Or tensor of
738	                shape (batch_size, n_queries, d_model).
739	            mask_feats (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size,
740	                each of shape (n_points_i, d_model).
741	
742	        Returns:
743	            Tuple:
744	                List[Tensor]: Classification predictions of len batch_size,
745	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_instance_classes + 1).
746	                List[Tensor] or None: Semantic predictions of len batch_size,
747	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_semantic_classes + 1).
748	                List[Tensor]: Confidence scores of len batch_size,
749	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, 1).
750	                List[Tensor]: Predicted masks of len batch_size,
751	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_points_i).
752	                List[Tensor] or None: Attention masks of len batch_size,
753	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_points_i).
754	        """
755	        cls_preds, sem_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks = \
756	            [], [], [], [], []
757	        for i in range(len(queries)):
758	            norm_query = self.out_norm(queries[i])
759	            if not self.sphere_cls:
760	                cls_preds.append(self.out_cls(norm_query))
761	                if last_flag:
762	                    sem_preds.append(self.out_sem(norm_query))
763	     
764	            pred_score = self.out_score(norm_query) if self.objectness_flag \
765	                else None
766	            pred_scores.append(pred_score)
767	            pred_mask = torch.einsum('nd,md->nm', norm_query, mask_feats[i])
768	            
769	            if self.sphere_cls:

771	                
772	                maskpool_embd = self.mask_pooling_proj(maskpool_) 
773	                cls_embd = self.cls_proj(maskpool_embd + norm_query) 
774	                cls_pred = self.forward_logit(cls_embd) 
775	                cls_preds.append(cls_pred)
776	                if last_flag:
777	                    norm_query_sem = norm_query.clone()
778	                    maskpool_embd_sem  = self.mask_pooling_proj_sem(maskpool_)
779	                    cls_embd_sem = self.cls_proj_sem(maskpool_embd_sem + norm_query_sem)
780	                    cls_pred_sem = self.forward_logit(cls_embd_sem, sem=True)
781	                    sem_preds.append(cls_pred_sem)
782	                
783	            if self.attn_mask:
784	                attn_mask = (pred_mask.sigmoid() < 0.5).bool()
785	                attn_mask[torch.where(
786	                    attn_mask.sum(-1) == attn_mask.shape[-1])] = False
787	                attn_mask = attn_mask.detach()
788	                attn_masks.append(attn_mask)
789	            pred_masks.append(pred_mask)
790	        attn_masks = attn_masks if self.attn_mask else None
791	        sem_preds = sem_preds if last_flag else None
792	        return cls_preds, sem_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks

821	    def forward_iter_pred(self, x, queries, interaction_masks=None):

824	        Args:

826	                (n_points_i, in_channels).

1050	    def get_query_tokens(self, hidden_states, input_ids, text, num_qa):
1051	        """
1052	        Extract query tokens from hidden_states, grouped by QA pair.
1053	
1054	        Following preprocess_chatml's rounds splitting, determine the token range of each
1055	        assistant reply, then extract embeddings between <p>...</p> within that range.
1056	
1057	        Args:
1058	            hidden_states: hidden states of the model's last layer, shape (1, seq_len, hidden_dim)
1059	            input_ids: input token ids, shape (1, seq_len)
1060	            text: full text after apply_chat_template
1061	            num_qa: number of QA pairs
1062	
1063	        Returns:
1064	            list of query tokens, length num_qa, each element is a (num_queries, hidden_dim) tensor
1065	        """
1066	        hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape[-1]
1067	        device = hidden_states.device
1068	        tokenizer = self.processor.tokenizer
1069	
1070	        # get ids of special tokens
1071	        p_start_id = self.seg_tokens_ids[0]  # <p>
1072	        p_end_id = self.seg_tokens_ids[1]    # </p>
1073	
1074	        input_ids_flat = input_ids[0]  # (seq_len,)
1075	        hidden_flat = hidden_states[0]  # (seq_len, hidden_dim)
1076	
1077	        # find positions of all <p> and </p>
1078	        p_start_positions = (input_ids_flat == p_start_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
1079	        p_end_positions = (input_ids_flat == p_end_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
1080	
1081	        # follow preprocess_chatml splitting
1082	        conv = get_conv('chatml', qwen_model=self.base_model)
1083	        rounds = [m + conv.seps[0] for m in text.split(conv.seps[0])]
1084	        rounds = rounds[:-1]  # drop the final empty round
1085	
1086	        # grouping: system + user + assistant as one group, then every two (user + assistant) as a group
1087	        if conv.system is None:
1088	            grouped_rounds = [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(0, len(rounds), 2)]
1089	        else:
1090	            grouped_rounds = [''.join(rounds[:3])] + [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(3, len(rounds), 2)]
1091	
1092	        # separator: used to split instruction and assistant reply
1093	        sep = conv.seps[0] + conv.roles[1]  # '<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'
1094	
1095	        all_query_tokens = []
1096	        cur_len = 0
1097	
1098	        for i, rou in enumerate(grouped_rounds):
1099	            if i >= num_qa:
1100	                break
1101	            if len(rou) == 0:
1102	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1103	                continue
1104	
1105	            # compute the token length of this round
1106	            rou_len = tokenizer(rou, return_length=True).length[0]
1107	
1108	            # split instruction and assistant reply
1109	            parts = rou.split(sep)
1110	            if len(parts) < 2:
1111	                # no assistant reply
1112	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1113	                cur_len += rou_len
1114	                continue
1115	
1116	            ins = sep.join(parts[:-1]) + sep
1117	            ins_len = tokenizer(ins, return_length=True).length[0]
1118	
1119	            # token range of assistant reply
1120	            assistant_start = cur_len + ins_len
1121	            assistant_end = cur_len + rou_len
1122	
1123	            # find <p>...</p> within this range
1124	            qa_queries = []
1125	            used_end_positions = set()
1126	
1127	            for p_start in p_start_positions:
1128	                if p_start < assistant_start or p_start >= assistant_end:
1129	                    continue
1130	
1131	                # find matching </p>
1132	                for p_end in p_end_positions:
1133	                    if p_end > p_start and p_end <= assistant_end and p_end not in used_end_positions:
1134	                        used_end_positions.add(p_end)
1135	
1136	                        # extract token embeddings between <p> and </p>
1137	                        if p_end > p_start + 1:
1138	                            between_embeddings = hidden_flat[p_start + 1 : p_end]
1139	                            avg_embedding = between_embeddings.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
1140	                            qa_queries.append(avg_embedding)
1141	                        break
1142	
1143	            if len(qa_queries) > 0:
1144	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.cat(qa_queries[:2], dim=0)) # only use the first 2 query tokens
1145	            else:
1146	                # this QA has no <p>...</p>, return NaN
1147	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1148	
1149	            cur_len += rou_len
1150	
1151	        # if grouped_rounds count is less than num_qa, pad with NaN
1152	        while len(all_query_tokens) < num_qa:
1153	            all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1154	        all_query_tokens = torch.cat(all_query_tokens, dim=0)
1155	        return all_query_tokens
